paper.title: Designing Decision Support Systems Using Counterfactual Prediction Sets

settings.name_in_paper: Finding the optimal conformal predictor (arms = alpha values in A) with counterfactual monotonicity
unmapped: Arms are m nested conformal prediction sets (K = m = calibration set size); the feature x_t and label y_t are observed each round, allowing counterfactual inference of rewards of other arms
Counterfactual monotonicity assumption on the expert's predictions (structural causal model): success with a set implies success with any smaller set still containing the label
settings.definition_quote: In our problem, each arm corresponds to a different parameter value $\alpha$ and, at each round $t$, a (potentially different) human expert receives a sample with feature vector $x_t$, picks a label value $\hat{y}_t$ from the prediction set $\Ccal_{\alpha_t}(x_t)$ provided by the conformal predictor with $\alpha_t \in \Acal$, and obtains a reward $\II\{ \hat{y}_t = y_t \} \in \{0, 1\}$. Here, we observe $x_t$ at the beginning of each round and $y_t$ and $\II\{ \hat{y}_t = y_t \}$ at the end of each round.

conditions: T >= sqrt(m) where m = K is the calibration set size / number of arms
nested prediction sets from a conformal predictor
tuning: confidence radius sqrt(2 log T / nu(alpha))

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Given a calibration set $\Dcal_{\text{cal}} = \{ (x_i, y_i) \}_{i=1}^{m}$ and a maximum number of rounds $T \geq \sqrt{m}$, Counterfactual SE is guaranteed to achieve expected regret $\EE[R(t)] \leq O \left( \sqrt{t \log m \log T} \right)$ for any $t \leq T$.

results.notes: Paper's m (number of calibration points = number of arms) mapped to K. Regret defined via expected accuracies, so pseudo-regret. Holds under counterfactual monotonicity.

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit with m arms (vanilla, no counterfactual inference)
